name: Pulle Dominoes
description: Pulle is a four-player block domino game from Austria using a double-8 set of 36 tiles (doubles removed). Players contribute an equal stake to the pool (Pulle). Each round, unplayed pip counts are added to running scores; players exceeding 100 are eliminated. Last survivor wins the pool. Buy-back and broken-pool rules apply.

content.text: Pulle is a four-player block domino game from Austria using a double-8 set of 36 tiles (doubles removed). Players contribute an equal stake to the pool (Pulle). Each round, unplayed pip counts are added to running scores; players exceeding 100 are eliminated. Last survivor wins the pool. Buy-back and broken-pool rules apply.
Austrian domino variant; described in Domino in vielen Spielarten (Fritz Beck, Vienna, 1960). Traditionally played for money.
Four players play as individuals. Each receives seven tiles from a 36-tile set (double-8 with nine doubles removed). No boneyard is used; it is a block game.
Double-8 set with nine doubles removed (36 tiles).
Double-8 domino set; optional stakes for the pool.
Each player receives 7 tiles. No boneyard is used (block game). First round: holder of heaviest tile leads; thereafter the winner of the previous round leads.

items.text: Per-game payment: Winner of each round receives an amount from each opponent (e.g. 1.00 each); blocked-game winner receives half (e.g. 0.50 each). Tied blocked game: no payment, pip totals not added to running scores.
